description: extract the shared normalize/index/fraction preamble from Lut3D.LookupTrilinear and LookupTetrahedral
reason: Type-1 clone of ~22 lines, but it is entirely float arithmetic whose output is compared numerically by Lut3DTests. scoring.md sets a risk floor of 8 for that, so even at confidence 1.0 the score stays under threshold. The extraction is almost certainly safe (expressions move verbatim, all operands stay float, no reassociation); it is the instrument, not the edit, that is missing. Revisit only if per-entry golden LUT hashes are added for the trilinear and tetrahedral paths.

description: unify the calibration-pipeline tail in ColorAdjustments.ApplyUserAdjustmentsLinear (607-631) with GetAppliedWhiteShapeMultipliers (731-747)
reason: Type-3, and the divergence is deliberate and documented: GetAppliedWhiteShapeMultipliers omits the RGB offsets and the final clamp on purpose (its doc comment explains that an additive lift is zero for the white-shape question it answers), and the two sites pass different NightBasis values. Unifying needs at least two axes of parameterization, which clone-taxonomy.md says means the clones have earned their separation. Plus the float risk floor of 8.

description: extract the shared 'apply calibration adjustments' block in LutGenerator (258-283 and 536-562)
reason: Near-identical 12-line block, but it sits inside two different generation loops whose surrounding math differs (one PQ-encodes directly, the other then does a measured-response inverse lookup). Float risk floor of 8 applies and the value is only ~12 SLOC. Not worth the indirection into a hot per-entry loop (card row 20).

Type-2 with asymmetric differences: MeasureSpectralAsync additionally resets _spectralXyz/_spectralValues/_spectralExpectedCount under the lock, the two use different TaskCompletionSource generic types and different pending fields, and the log and timeout messages differ. It also touches cancellation, locking and process lifetime (card rows 8, 9, 10). Asymmetric Type-2 means escalate, not refactor.

description: deduplicate the property blocks shared by CalibrationSettings and SettingsManager.MonitorProfileData
reason: Type-0: these are auto-property declaration lists with initializers, which is the language's grammar, not duplication (57 lines carrying only 110 tokens). They are also two different serialization shapes - MonitorProfileData is the persisted per-monitor JSON. Unifying them would couple the settings file format to the in-memory model (card row 11).

description: extract a shared button/panel factory from DisplayMatchWindow and ReportHistoryWindow
reason: Type-0 WPF code-behind construction grammar. Both windows already have a local Make() helper; hoisting it to a shared base or utility for exactly two call sites is the premature-generic anti-lever. No test coverage for WPF window construction either, so it is unverifiable at any confidence.

description: deduplicate the shared header/nav/footer blocks across site/index.html, guides.html, whitepaper.html and 404.html
reason: Real duplication (90, 58, 54, 33, 29, 28, 25-line blocks), but site/ is static HTML with no test suite and no goldens whatsoever. Confidence is structurally zero: nothing in this repo would tell me if a templating change altered a rendered page. Needs a static-render golden (hash the built output of each page) before it is even scorable.

description: remove the 56 swallowed exception handlers flagged by the swallow-except probe
reason: Out of scope by construction, not by risk. pathologies.md #2 is explicit: removing a swallow turns a silent no-op into a propagating throw, which is usually the correct behavior but is emphatically not isomorphic. That is a bug-fix pass and belongs outside this ledger. Reported to the user separately.

description: act on the 198 jscpd clone pairs involving publish-joint-hdr/, publish-ui-polish/, Releases-*/ and ReleasesNew/
reason: Not source. These are untracked build/publish output trees (Gloam.deps.json, README.md, LICENSE.txt, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt copies) that dominate the clone report by line count. The four dirs are untracked and unlike publish/ and Releases/ they are not covered by .gitignore, which is why they leak into the survey.

description: parameterize ColorMath.GamutCoverage and GamutCoverageUv over a chromaticity-mapping function
reason: Genuine Type-2 differing on exactly one axis (raw xy vs ToUvPrime), so it is structurally legal to unify with a Func<Chromaticity,(double,double)>. Rejected on the float risk floor of 8: both return gamut-coverage percentages that tests compare numerically, and the win is only ~10 SLOC. Passing a delegate per vertex also trades a direct call for an indirect one in the coverage path. Revisit if gamut-coverage goldens are added.

description: extract the shared preset preamble in PatchSetGenerator (GenerateCustomSet / GenerateQuickSet / GenerateGrayscaleSet)
reason: The residue of an already-correct factoring, not duplication to remove. The real work is in shared helpers (CreatePatch, AddGrayscaleRamp, AddPrimariesAndSecondaries, AddGrid, FinalizePatchSet); what jscpd matches is the 4-line list/index preamble plus the Black and White reference patches. The presets then diverge on point count, grid size, and finalization (drift anchors vs dedupe+reindex) - two or more axes. Extracting the preamble would be the helper-for-grammar anti-lever.

description: hoist the SafeChromaticity/SafeNonNegative/SafePositive/SafeGamma sanitizers shared by CalibrationProfile, CalibrationReport and DisplayCalibrationProfile
reason: Two-line expression-bodied guards, each taking a caller-supplied fallback that differs per site. Value is only ~3 (leaf helpers nobody reads), and a shared sanitizer class would need every call site to keep passing its own fallback anyway, so the indirection buys nothing. Scores under threshold; not a hazard because there is no shared invariant between the copies the way there was for the CGATS quoting or the CIE table.

description: deduplicate the remaining ~20 clone pairs in tests/Gloam.Tests and the WPF window code-behind
reason: Type-0 across the board: table-driven test arrange blocks (CalibrationMetricsTests, ClosedLoopCorrectorTests, HdrMhc2Lut*, AdvancedColorProfileMigration vs IccColorManagementRegression) and WPF construction grammar (CalibrationReportWindow, ProfileManagerWindow, ReportHistoryWindow, DisplayMatchWindow). Test setup that looks alike is usually two tests deliberately pinning the same scenario from different angles; collapsing it couples them and makes a future divergence silently untestable. clone-taxonomy.md: leave Type-0 alone, raise the threshold instead.
